t: You are standing where the Mappin and Webb Building once stood, at the meeting of Queen Victoria Street and Poultry, close to Bank Junction. It was a Grade II listed building, put up in 1871 and demolished in 1994 along with eight or nine other listed buildings, to make way for the office building No. 1 Poultry. Many people consider it the most significant of those losses. It was designed by John Belcher, an English architect who became president of the Royal Institute of British Architects.
